description: Two-panel composite of horizontal grouped bar charts reporting yield stress measured at 800 °C. Both panels share the x-axis 'Yield stress [MPa]' with labelled ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120 and 140, and an identical legend box listing dark grey as '(in compression)' and light grey as '(in tension)'. Panel (a) gives five Fe–15Al-based alloys, labelled top to bottom Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C and Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C. Panel (b) gives seven Fe–26Al-based alloys: Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C and Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C. In every alloy the dark compression bar is longer than the paired light tension bar. The carbide/Laves-forming additions raise yield stress: in (a) the Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C compression bar reaches just past the 100 MPa gridline; in (b) Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C is strongest overall, its compression bar ending between the 120 and 140 MPa gridlines. No numeric values are printed on any bar, so only gridline positions are readable. The figure demonstrates tension–compression asymmetry of the yield stress at 800 °C for all alloys.

observations.observation: Both panels are horizontal grouped bar charts with x-axis labelled 'Yield stress [MPa]' and printed ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120 and 140.
Each panel contains a legend box giving dark grey bars as '(in compression)' and light grey bars as '(in tension)'.
For every alloy in both panels the dark grey compression bar is longer than the paired light grey tension bar, i.e. the compression/tension gap is present for all twelve alloy conditions shown.
Panel (a) lists, top to bottom, Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C.
Panel (b) lists, top to bottom, Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C.

In panel (a) the Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C pair has the longest bars, with the compression bar ending just beyond the 100 MPa gridline, whereas unalloyed Fe-15Al has the shortest bars (compression bar between the 20 and 40 MPa gridlines).
In panel (b) Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C has the longest compression bar in the whole figure, ending between the 120 and 140 MPa gridlines, while Fe-26Al has the shortest pair.
In both panels the 2Nb-1C and 2Ta-1C alloys show clearly longer compression bars than the 2Ti-1C and 2V-1C alloys of the same base composition.

In panel (b) the 4 at.% additions (Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C) give longer compression bars than their 2 at.% counterparts (Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C), showing a composition-dependent increase.
No numeric value labels are printed on any bar; values can only be read against the 20 MPa gridlines.
The caption states that the plotted yield stresses are those measured at 800 °C in compression and in tension, for Fe–15Al-based (a) and Fe–26Al-based (b) alloys.

The citing text states that comparison of yield stress in compression and tension at 650 °C (Fig. 7) and at 800 °C (Fig. 8) confirms asymmetric tension–compression behaviour of all investigated alloys at both temperatures.

The citing text states that room-temperature mechanical testing already revealed a significant tension–compression asymmetry, which motivated testing in tension at 650 and 800 °C as possible application temperatures.

subfigures.description: Horizontal grouped bar chart for five Fe–15Al-based alloys (Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C) at 800 °C; x-axis 'Yield stress [MPa]' 0–140 with ticks every 20; legend: dark grey '(in compression)', light grey '(in tension)'. In all five alloys the compression bar exceeds the tension bar; the longest pair belongs to Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C, whose compression bar passes the 100 MPa gridline.

Horizontal grouped bar chart for seven Fe–26Al-based alloys (Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C) at 800 °C; same x-axis and legend as (a). Compression bars again exceed tension bars for every alloy; Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C shows the largest compression value, its bar ending between the 120 and 140 MPa gridlines, and Fe-26Al (no carbide addition) the smallest.
